was: City of Jacksonville facility (Better Jacksonville Plan, opened 2004; day-to-day run by NE Florida Equestrian Society concessionaire). ~70 full-service pull-through big-rig sites (30/50A); open to non-equestrian transient campers year-round subject to availability (book the Non-Event option); a reviewer parked a 32-ft rig. Reservable online via RoverPass plus the official form. RV Life $$$, 5 stars. --Claude
note: City of Jacksonville equestrian center at 13611 Normandy Blvd, run since 2014 by the non-profit Northeast Florida Equestrian Society.  Its RV lots, where no horses are allowed, have 30/50-amp full-hookup sites, some pull-through, 50-amp water-and-electric overflow sites and primitive sites, each listed at 40 ft.  An outside restroom with showers by the main arena is open around the clock, and there is a dump station; swimming and fishing are prohibited on the property. --Claude

was: Small rural campsite (~5 spacious, level pull-thru sites; big-rig friendly, fits trailers over 40 ft) on a meadow by the Black River near Edwards. 30-amp $35 / 50-amp $40 / primitive $20; hot showers, flush toilets, river+pond fishing (no license), kayaking. Book by request/approval via Hipcamp or RoverPass.
note: Small campground on a meadow at 20450 Old Hwy 80, Edwards, between the Black River, a fishing pond, a farm and a forest, reached by an unlit dirt road off I-20's exit 19: 30/50-amp RV sites on grass and gravel, pull-throughs among them, plus primitive RV and tent sites.  There are hot showers and flush toilets but no dump station, the nearest being 8 miles away; the river and pond can be fished without a license, and the river kayaked.  Its Hipcamp listing no longer takes bookings. --Claude

was: Lisbon Park District park on the Sheyenne River (Ransom County). 16 full RV hookups (10x 30-amp, 6x 50-amp) plus a North Campground (electric-only, behind the FEMA dike) and primitive grass tent sites. Electric sites are prepaid/reserved (self-service, also on RoverPass); primitive is FCFS via payment slips at the showerhouse. Outdoor pool, mini golf, ball complex, showers. --Claude
note: Lisbon Park District park on the Sheyenne River, open April 1 to November 14: a West Campground of full-hookup sites and a North Campground behind the FEMA dike with electric and water, every site wired for 20, 30 and 50 amps, plus primitive camping on the grass.  The campground is self-service: hookup sites must be reserved and paid ahead, while primitive sites are first come, first served.  There are showerhouses and a dump station, and the park has an outdoor pool, mini golf, a skate park, ball fields and courts. --Claude

was: 27-acre Barnes County park in the wooded Sheyenne River valley, 4 mi S + 1 mi E of Kathryn on Hwy 46 (Sheyenne River Valley Scenic Byway). 34 campsites: 16 electric (lower area, fit RVs) and 18 secluded primitive upper sites better for tents/small campers; hiking trails and footbridges over a spring-fed stream. Open May 1-Oct 31; reservable online. --Claude
note: Barnes County's 27-acre park in the hills along the Sheyenne River, 4 miles south and 1 mile east of Kathryn on Highway 46, on the Sheyenne River Valley National Scenic Byway, open May 1 to October 31: 34 campsites, 16 with electric and 18 more secluded primitive sites in the upper part of the park, suited to tents and small campers.  Every site must be reserved, for a week at most.  There are three concrete vault toilets, rural water for filling tanks, a dump station, a playground, and hiking trails with footbridges over a spring-fed stream. --Claude
